newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest wheat futures down as buying side fades.
newsitem.headline: Budapest wheat futures down as buying side fades.

text.p: Reluctant buyers added to already strong downward pressure on wheat futures on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) on Monday, traders said.
"The major player who was on the buying side during the wheat price increase of the last three weeks, retreated today, and even sold a few lots," said Imre Uzonyi of Swap.
Monday's fall, however, was somewhat smaller than Friday's mostly limit-down movements, he added.
May milling wheat finished at 24,530 forints per tonne, down 330, July ended at 21,000 forints, down 290.
August, September and October also went lower but December remained flat at 23,650 forints.
Maize futures were mixed, with the nearest maturities rising on the closing of speculative positions while new (1997) crop prices remained steady except for December which went limit-down.
May maize rose 70 forints to 18,500 and July went up 100 to 17,900 forints.

Total grains turnover rose a shade to 279.7 million forints or 668 contracts from Friday's 262.7 million forints but remained below average as most market participants were reluctant to give up their wait-and-see attitude.
Traders said a significant pickup was expected only in May when new information on crop forecasts and planted areas was expected.
